79: 
80: ## RULE 1: Identity Anchor Block
81: 
82: **Why:** The AI model has no memory between clip generations. Even with @ingredient tags, the model can drift on details (adding moustache, changing skin tone, altering clothing). The identity anchor TEXT reinforces the visual reference.
83: 
84: **The rule:** Every prompt must include a `character.identity` field with a frozen 2-3 line physical description. This description must match the uploaded ingredient image exactly. Include the `character.enforce` field that explicitly tells the model not to deviate.
85: 
86: **What the identity block must contain:**
87: - Face shape (sharp jawline, round face, high cheekbones)
88: - Eye details (color, shape, expression style)
89: - Skin tone (specific: medium-brown, dark, fair, weathered)
90: - Hair (color, length, style — tied bun, loose, messy)
91: - Facial hair (MUST explicitly state: no moustache / thick black moustache / clean-shaven)
92: - Build (lean, muscular, heavy, thin)
93: 
94: **The enforce line (copy exactly):**
95: ```
96: IDENTITY LOCK: This character must match the uploaded @[TagName] reference image exactly. The text description above is a verified match to that reference. Do not alter face shape, skin tone, facial features, hair style, or clothing.
97: ```
98: 
99: ---
100: 
101: ## RULE 2: Environment Anchor Block
102: 
103: **Why:** Environments drift too — lighting changes, room layout shifts, props disappear between shots.
104: 
105: **The rule:** Every prompt must include `environment.tag` (the @ingredient name) plus `environment.description` (frozen physical details) plus `environment.enforce` (assertion that the text matches the ingredient).
106: 
107: **What the environment block must contain:**
108: - Wall/floor material and condition (mud walls, marble floor)
109: - Specific props (UPSC books, broken suitcase, luxury car)
110: - Color palette (vibrant village colors, sterile white office)
111: - Atmosphere detail (sunlight streaming in, rain pouring outside)
112: 
113: ---
114: 
115: ## RULE 3: Forcing / Constraint Reinforcement
116: 
117: **Why:** Tagging alone (@AnjaliStudent) gives the model a reference but no assertion of how seriously to follow it. Adding explicit constraint lines forces compliance.
118: 
119: **Three enforcement lines to use (adapt per character):**
120: 
121: 1. **Identity Lock** (in character.enforce):
122: ```
123: IDENTITY LOCK: This character must match the uploaded @[TagName] reference image exactly. The text description above is a verified match to that reference. Do not alter face shape, skin tone, facial features, hair style, or clothing.
124: ```
125: 
126: 2. **Continuity Assertion** (when same character appears across consecutive shots):
127: ```
128: CONTINUITY: This character appeared in the previous shot with identical face and clothing. Maintain absolute visual continuity.
129: ```
130: 
131: 3. **Negative Constraints** (in negative_constraints field):
132: ```

138: ## RULE 4: Hinglish Dialogue + Voice Assignment
139: 
140: **Why:** English dialogue descriptions generate nothing useful. Actual Hinglish dialogue in the prompt produces natural speech. Voice name forces consistent character voice.

142: **The rules:**
143: - The `audio.dialogue.line` field must contain dialogue in **Hinglish** (Hindi-English mix, natural spoken style)
144: - All other JSON fields (camera, lighting, action, style) remain in English
145: - Add `voice` field with Gemini voice name + style tags
146: - Max 1-2 sentences per clip for natural speech pacing
147: - **DO NOT write English descriptions of what the character says** — write the actual dialogue
148: - **DO NOT include lip_sync_note or voice_mod fields** — removed from pipeline

150: **Example:**

154:   "line": "Aaj tumne mujhe ghar se nikala hai. Ek din isi darwaze par IAS ban kar aaungi.",

156: }

171: 
172: **Why:** When narrator is speaking, character mouths should stay closed. Narrator voiceover is added in post-production via ElevenLabs — Flow should generate silent characters.
173: 
174: **The rules:**
175: - **NO lip_sync_note field** — removed from pipeline entirely
176: - **NO voice_mod field** — replaced by `voice` field with Gemini voice name
177: - When narrator speaks → character has no dialogue in Flow. Narrator audio is post-production.
178: - When character speaks → write actual Hinglish dialogue + assign voice name

182: ## RULE 6: Negative Constraints
183: 
184: **Why:** Without explicit "do NOT" instructions, the model adds default details — random jewelry, facial hair, extra people, text overlays, or defaults to moody lighting.
185: 
186: **Standard negative constraints (adapt per shot):**
187: ```json

No extra characters not named in this prompt. No changing the character's clothing, hair, or skin tone from the reference. No cartoon physics. No dark, gloomy, or moody lighting."
189: ```

193: ## RULE 7: Policy-Safe Framing
194: 
195: **Why:** Google Flow blocks prompts that reference real public figures, graphic violence, or sensitive content without fictional framing. Extreme poverty, domestic conflict, and humiliation can sometimes trigger safety flags.
196: 
197: **The rule:** Every prompt must begin with the `policy_frame` field:
198: ```json
199: "policy_frame": "Scene from a fictional Hindi cinematic drama film. All characters, names, locations, and events are entirely fictional. No real persons are depicted."
200: ```
201: 
202: **Additional safety for emotional/domestic conflict scenes (kicking out, humiliation):**
203: ```json
204: "policy_frame": "Scene from a fictional Hindi cinematic drama film. This scene depicts a fictional emotional disagreement between characters — no graphic violence, abuse, or explicit content is shown. All characters and events are entirely fictional."
205: ```
206: 
207: ---
208: 
209: ## RULE 8: Slow-Motion and Speed Instructions
210: 
211: **Why:** Slow-motion and speed ramping stretch clip runtime (important for 15+ minute videos) and add dramatic weight to key moments. These must be specified IN the prompt, not added in post.
212: 
213: **Normal speed (default):**
214: ```json
215: "speed": "Normal playback speed."
216: ```
217: 
218: **Full slow-motion:**
219: ```json
220: "speed": "Slow-motion 0.5x throughout the entire clip. All movement plays at half speed."
221: ```
222: 
223: **Speed ramp (normal → slow at impact):**
224: ```json
225: "speed": "Normal speed 0-4s. At the moment of impact (4s), ramp to slow-motion 0.5x for the remaining 4-8s."
226: ```
227: 
228: ---
229: 
230: ## RULE 9: Audio and SFX Direction
231: 
232: **Why:** Without explicit audio direction, the AI model either generates no sound or generates random ambient noise that doesn't match the scene.
233: 
234: **The rule:** Every prompt must include the `audio` block with three sub-fields:
235: 
236: 1. **ambient** — continuous background sound (hum, rain, wind, distant traffic)
237: 2. **sfx** — specific sound events tied to moments (door slam at 2s, glass breaking at 5s)
238: 3. **dialogue** — character speech with speaker tag, Hindi line, and voice modifier
239: 
240: **Example for a study scene:**
241: ```json
242: "audio": {
243:   "ambient": "Heavy rain falling on a tin roof. Distant thunder rumbling.",
244:   "sfx": "Pages of a heavy book turning at 1s. Pen scratching on paper at 6s.",
245:   "dialogue": {
246:     "speaker": "NARRATOR (off-screen)",
247:     "line": "No dialogue.",
248:     "voice": "NONE"
249:   }
250: }
251: ```
252: 
253: ---
254: 
255: ## RULE 10: Weight-at-Start
256: 
257: **Why:** The AI model pays more attention to the first 30-40% of the prompt. Subject and action must lead. Style and quality modifiers go last.
258: 
259: **The rule:** Order the JSON fields in this priority:
260: 1. `policy_frame` (first — sets the context)
261: 2. `character` (identity is the most important constraint)
262: 3. `environment` (where this happens)
263: 4. `action` (what happens, per-second breakdown)
264: 5. `camera` (how it's filmed)
265: 6. `lighting` (atmosphere)
266: 7. `audio` (sound design)
267: 8. `speed` (playback speed)
268: 9. `style` (quality, color grade — last)
269: 10. `negative_constraints` (what to avoid — last)
270: 
271: ---
272: 
273: ## RULE 11: No Contradictions
274: 
275: **Why:** When the prompt contains contradictory instructions, the model picks the strongest signal and ignores the rest. This produces unexpected results.
276: 
277: **Common contradictions to avoid:**
278: - "Static camera" + "push-in movement" → pick one
279: - "Close-up of face" + "wide shot showing full room" → one shot type per clip
280: - "She is frozen still" + "she runs to the door" → in different time segments is fine, as simultaneous instruction it contradicts
